rules.compost: Food scraps, food-soiled paper, coffee grounds, plant and yard debris. Only items labeled BPI Certified or CMA can be composted.
rules.plastic: Rigid plastic containers go in the container and bottle recycling cart. Empty and rinse. Plastic bags and film go in the landfill container.
rules.paper: Clean, dry paper, cardboard and molded fiber go in the paper and cardboard recycling cart. Paper towels and paper cups do not. Juice and milk boxes go in the landfill container.
rules.glass: Glass bottles and jars go in the container and bottle recycling cart. Rinse clean. Dishware, ceramics and window glass do not belong in recycling.
rules.landfill: Plastic bags and film, foam, juice and milk boxes, diapers and pet waste. Hazardous and electronic waste go to an Alameda County hazardous waste facility.

rules.compost: Food scraps, food-soiled and waxy paper, plants, and plastic labeled compostable go in the green bin.
rules.plastic: Clean, empty plastic containers go in the blue bin. Check SFRecycles.org for film and flexible plastics.
rules.paper: Clean, dry paper and cardboard go in the blue bin, including empty paper cups. Food-soiled paper goes in the green bin.
rules.glass: Empty glass bottles and jars go in the blue bin. Rinse them first.
rules.landfill: Only what cannot be recycled or composted goes in the black bin. Styrofoam cannot go in the blue or green bins.

rules.compost: Food scraps, food-soiled paper and yard debris go in the compost cart. Do not bag them in plastic bags.
rules.plastic: Rinse plastic bottles and containers and place them in the recycling cart. Toys, single-use utensils, plates, cups, straws, hangers and hoses are not accepted.
rules.paper: Clean paper and cardboard go in the recycling cart. Food-soiled paper goes in the compost cart.
rules.glass: Glass bottles and jars go in the recycling cart. Rinse them first.
rules.landfill: Anything that cannot be recycled or composted goes in the trash cart. Clothing does not belong in the recycling cart.

rules.compost: Food scraps can go in your garbage cart. The city sorts and composts them. Yard trimmings go loose in the street or in the optional yard trimmings cart.
rules.plastic: Clean, empty plastic containers go in the blue recycling cart. Check SanJoseRecycles.org for bags and film.
rules.paper: Clean paper and cardboard go in the blue recycling cart (single-stream).
rules.glass: Glass bottles and jars go in the blue recycling cart.
rules.landfill: Garbage goes in the garbage cart. Batteries, paint, medicine and other household hazardous waste must not go in garbage or recycling.

rules.compost: Put food scraps in a clear plastic bag in the food side of your split cart or your food-only cart. Compostable or paper bags are fine.
rules.plastic: Rinse plastic containers and place them in the recycling cart. Metal cans and clean foil go in the recycling cart. Plastic bags can be recycled at grocery stores.
rules.paper: Flatten cardboard boxes and keep paper clean. Remove inserts from paper boxes.
rules.glass: Glass bottles and jars go in the recycling cart. Empty and rinse containers, put lids back on.
rules.landfill: Place these items in your split garbage cart or garbage bin. Hazardous waste, electronics, and batteries must be taken to a household hazardous waste facility.
